mission.quote:
Dance is not movement.
It is story.
mission.body1: Based in New Jersey, Choomnoori Korean Traditional Dance Academy is a cultural arts education organization that carries the spirit and values of Korean traditional arts to the next generation.
mission.body2: Students learn more than technique. Through breath, emotion, etiquette, and focus, they discover self-expression and cultural identity through dance.
mission.body3: At Choomnoori, classes, performances, and cultural experiences are connected. Children learn patience through movement, confidence through the stage, and their roots through tradition.
mission.body4: Choomnoori serves as a bridge for Korean culture in American society, continuing a wide range of activities to preserve authentic Korean traditional arts and share their value with local communities.
mission.body5: For Korean communities in the United States, Choomnoori also offers comfort, vitality, and lasting memories through traditional culture.

about.hero.description1: Choomnoori is a cultural arts education organization carrying the spirit and values of Korean traditional arts to the next generation. Students are guided to express themselves and discover cultural identity through dance.
about.director.bio1: Director Eun Hee Ahn is a traditional Korean performing artist and educator specializing in Korean dance and percussion. After graduating from Dankook University with a degree in Dance, she performed professionally with the Samsung Dance Company and now leads KTDOC as founder and artistic director, connecting education, performance, and cultural outreach.
about.director.bio.1: Eunhee Ahn graduated from the Department of Dance at Dankook University and trained in the Chae Hyang-soon style of Korean traditional dance. She currently serves as the New Jersey Branch Director of the Chae Hyang-soon Dance Preservation Society.
about.director.bio.2: In 2008, she founded the Korean Traditional Dance of Choomnoori (KTDOC) in New Jersey, where she has dedicated herself to teaching Korean traditional dance and percussion. She is also the Founder and President of the Korean Heritage Performing Arts Foundation (KHPAF), leading initiatives in arts education, international cultural exchange, and the development of the next generation of traditional performing artists.
about.director.bio.3: In addition to her performance career, she has presented hundreds of educational programs and cultural performances at public schools, museums, and community organizations throughout the United States, serving as a cultural ambassador dedicated to sharing Korea's rich artistic heritage with diverse audiences.
about.director.stages.title: Selected Venues
about.director.stages.lead: Throughout her career, Ms. Ahn has presented Korean traditional performing arts on prestigious stages in both the United States and Korea.
about.director.stages.1: NBC TODAY Show — 100-Day Countdown to the PyeongChang 2018 Olympic Winter Games
about.director.stages.2: United Nations Headquarters — Opening performance, Global Citizenship Education Event
about.director.stages.5: John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts
about.director.stages.6: Times Square, New York — National Heritage Campaign
about.director.awards.title: Awards
about.director.awards.1: 2023 New Jersey State Council on the Arts Individual Artist Fellowship in Choreography
about.staff.heading: Our Instructors
about.staff.baek.name: Soo Gyung Baek
about.staff.baek.bio1: Soo Gyung Baek earned her degree in Dance from the College of Arts at Kyungsung University in Korea. She brings extensive experience in dance education and arts administration, including serving as the owner and director of a dance academy in Korea from 1993 to 1996.
about.staff.baek.bio2: She currently serves as the Administrative Director and Instructor at Korean Traditional Dance of Choomnoori (KTDOC), where she supports educational programs, student development, and organizational operations. She also teaches Korean percussion and Nanta, sharing the energy and cultural heritage of Korean traditional performing arts with the next generation.
about.staff.baek.career.title: Professional Background
about.staff.baek.career.1: B.A. in Dance, College of Arts, Kyungsung University, Korea
about.staff.baek.career.4: Nanta & Korean Drum Instructor, Pilgrim Korean School
about.staff.han.name: Jinseon Han
about.staff.han.bio1: Jinseon Han studied Dance at the Korea National University of Arts and has trained in Korean dance from an early age. Since 2021, she has continued her training in Korean traditional dance and percussion under Director Eunhee Ahn.
about.staff.han.bio2: She participated in the 2022 Alvin Ailey performance Connecting Hope and received the Grand Prize in Modeumbuk at the World Korean Traditional Music Competition in 2023. She has teaching experience at Korean heritage schools, including in Montclair, as well as cultural arts assemblies in U.S. public schools. She currently serves as an Assistant Instructor at KTDOC.

pages.calendar.title: Get academy events on your own device
pages.calendar.description: Subscribe once to our performances, events, and camps. When dates, times, or venues change, your Apple, Google, or Outlook calendar updates automatically.
pages.calendar.sub.guide.appleIos.title: iPhone · iPad (Apple Calendar)
pages.calendar.sub.guide.appleIos.body:
• Tap ‘Add to device calendar’ above to open the subscribe dialog. If it doesn’t open, use ‘Copy link’.
  • Go to Settings → Calendar → Accounts → Add Account → Other → Add Subscribed Calendar.
  • Paste the link and save.
pages.calendar.sub.guide.mac.title: Mac (Apple Calendar)
pages.calendar.sub.guide.mac.body:
• In Calendar, choose File → New Calendar Subscription.
  • Paste the link, subscribe, then pick an auto-refresh interval.
pages.calendar.sub.guide.google.title: Google Calendar
pages.calendar.sub.guide.google.body:
• Click ‘Add to Google Calendar’ (desktop recommended).
  • If it doesn’t open, go to Google Calendar → Other calendars + → From URL and paste the link.
  • Google may take up to 24 hours to refresh subscribed calendars.
pages.calendar.sub.guide.outlook.title: Outlook
pages.calendar.sub.guide.outlook.body:
• In Outlook Calendar, choose Add calendar → Subscribe from web.
  • Paste the link, name it, then import.
pages.calendar.sub.hint: Once subscribed, new performances, events, and camps — and any changes or cancellations — appear automatically. Timing depends on each calendar app’s refresh interval.
pages.sibguide.title: Registering Siblings Together
pages.sibguide.desc: One parent account is all you need, even with two or more children. Link all of your children as shown below, and you can follow every child’s classes and performances — and respond on their behalf — from a single account.
pages.sibguide.step1.title: New here? Add every child when you sign up
pages.sibguide.step1.body: Choose “Parent” on the sign-up page and child fields will appear. If you have more than one child, press “Add another child” and enter each name and enrollment year. A child links right away when their own student account already exists.
pages.sibguide.step1.caption: Sign-up screen — “Add another child” lets you enter every sibling at once.
pages.sibguide.step2.title: Already a member? Add children from My Profile
pages.sibguide.step2.body: After signing in, open “My Profile” in your member page and find the “My children” card. Press “Add child”, enter the name and enrollment year, and the request shows as “Awaiting review” until the studio confirms the link.
pages.sibguide.step2.caption: My Profile → My children — the studio confirms your request and completes the link.
pages.sibguide.step3.title: Once linked, here’s what you can do
pages.sibguide.step3.body: With your children linked, everything is organized per child in one account.
pages.sibguide.feat.classes.title: My Classes
pages.sibguide.feat.classes.body: Each child’s assigned classes appear in their own section.
pages.sibguide.feat.checkin.title: Performances
pages.sibguide.feat.checkin.body: Respond to performance participation (check-in) for each child on the performance page.
pages.sibguide.feat.calendar.title: Calendar
pages.sibguide.feat.calendar.body: Your children’s class schedules and performances they join (marked ✓) come together in one calendar.
pages.sibguide.feat.forms.title: Registration Forms
pages.sibguide.feat.forms.body: When filling out a registration form, simply pick the student from your children.
pages.sibguide.faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
pages.sibguide.faq1.q: My child hasn’t signed up yet.
pages.sibguide.faq1.a: Please create the child’s (student) account first — the name and enrollment year are how we match the link. Contact the studio if you need help.
pages.sibguide.faq2.a: For safety, the studio confirms every child link before it takes effect. If it’s taking long, please contact the studio.
pages.sibguide.faq3.q: I made a mistake / want to unlink.
pages.sibguide.faq3.a: Requests still “Awaiting review” can be deleted directly in “My children”. To remove a confirmed link, please ask the studio.

push.guide.title: About alerts
push.guide.whatP: They are short messages that appear on your phone screen for a moment. Think of them like a text from a friend arriving. They come even when this website isn't open, and even when your phone is locked.
push.guide.whatFree: They cost nothing, and you don't have to give us your phone number. They arrive over the internet, not as text messages.
push.guide.whenNote: We never send advertising. Only things you need to know.
push.guide.iosLede: On an iPhone, you must first add this site to your Home Screen as an app before alerts can arrive. That is Apple's rule. You only have to do it once.
push.guide.ios1: Open this website in Safari, then tap the button at the bottom centre that looks like a square with an arrow pointing up out of it.
push.guide.ios2: Scroll up the list and tap “Add to Home Screen”, then tap “Add”. A KTDOC icon appears on your Home Screen.
push.guide.ios3: Now open that new icon and tap “Turn on alerts”. (You must come in through the new icon, not through Safari.)
push.guide.ios4: When it asks whether to allow alerts, tap “Allow”. That's it.
push.guide.androidH: On an Android phone or a computer
push.guide.and2: A small box appears near the top of the screen asking whether to show notifications. Tap “Allow”. That's it.
push.guide.andNote: It only asks once. If you tapped “Block” by mistake, see “I'm not getting alerts” below.
push.guide.deviceH: Turn it on once on each device
push.guide.deviceP: Turning it on for your phone does not turn it on for your computer. Turn it on once on each device where you want alerts. For most people, a phone is enough.
push.guide.offP: You can turn them off at any time. Go to “My profile” in the left-hand menu and tap “Turn off alerts”. You turn them back on in the same place.
push.guide.trouble1: First, go to “My profile” and tap “Send me a test alert”. If that arrives, everything is set up properly.
push.guide.trouble2: On an iPhone, alerts won't arrive if you opened the site in Safari instead of the Home Screen icon. Please come in through the icon.
push.guide.trouble3: If you tapped “Block” by mistake — on iPhone go to Settings → Notifications → KTDOC; on Android or a computer, tap the lock at the left of the address bar → Notifications → Allow.
push.guide.trouble4: If your phone is on Do Not Disturb or silent, alerts arrive quietly. Swipe down to check your notification list.
push.guide.troubleTail: If it still doesn't work, please let the studio know. Nothing is lost — every alert also stays in “My alerts” in the left-hand menu.
